titulo: Hypotheses with «si»: Si + imperfect subjunctive: what you would do if…

aula.objetivo: Tell apart the three kinds of «si» sentences: a possible condition (si + present), an unlikely or unreal hypothesis about now (si + imperfecto de subjuntivo → conditional) and an impossible hypothesis about the past (si + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo → condicional compuesto), and give advice with «yo en tu lugar».

sessao.titulo: Si + imperfect subjunctive: what you would do if…

itens.pt: to learn to play an instrument

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «si» (no accent) is English "if". Good news: Spanish «si» sentences work almost exactly like the English first, second and third conditionals. The tense tells you how likely the condition is. STEP 2: there are three situations. (a) Possible: «Si tengo tiempo, voy» = "If I have time, I'll go" (session 2). (b) Unlikely or unreal now: «Si tuviera tiempo, iría» = "If I had time, I would go". (c) Impossible, in the past: «Si hubiera tenido tiempo, habría ido» = "If I had had time, I would have gone" (session 3). STEP 3: this session covers (b). English puts the "if" part in the past ("if I HAD"); Spanish puts it in the imperfecto de subjuntivo (lesson 46): «si tuviera», «si fuera», «si pudiera». STEP 4: the other part takes the simple conditional, English "would": infinitive + ía, ías, ía, íamos, íais, ían. «Viajaría, viajarías, viajaría, viajaríamos, viajaríais, viajarían.» STEP 5: some conditionals are irregular, with the same stem as the future: tendría, haría, diría, pondría, podría, querría, vendría, saldría, sabría, habría, valdría. STEP 6: never put the conditional in the «si» part — just as careful English avoids "if I would have money". «Si tendría dinero» is wrong; you may hear it in some regions, but standard Spanish avoids it. STEP 7: the two parts can swap places: «Viajaría más si tuviera dinero» = «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría más». If the «si» part comes first, use a comma. STEP 8: to give advice, use «Yo, en tu lugar, + conditional» or «Si yo fuera tú, + conditional» — English "If I were you…": «Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con él». The "were" is «fuera», never «era».
blocos.comparacao: English conditionals map neatly: "If I had money, I'd travel" = «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría»; "If I were you" = «Si yo fuera tú». Where English uses the past after "if", Spanish uses the past subjunctive; where English uses "would", Spanish uses the conditional. And the rule you already follow in English — no "would" after "if" — is strict in Spanish: never «si tendría».

exemplos.ru: Si ganara la lotería, dejaría el trabajo.
exemplos.pt: If I won the lottery, I'd quit my job.

exemplos.ru: Si tuviéramos más tiempo, daríamos la vuelta al mundo.
exemplos.pt: If we had more time, we'd go round the world.

exemplos.ru: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con ella.
exemplos.pt: If I were you, I'd talk to her.

exemplos.ru: Yo, en tu lugar, aceptaría el trabajo.
exemplos.pt: In your place, I'd take the job.

tabelas.titulo: Irregular conditionals (same stem as the future)

erros.motivo: The «si» part takes the imperfecto de subjuntivo, never the conditional (no "if I would have").
The other part takes the conditional; the subjunctive only goes in the «si» part.

erros.errado: Si yo era tú, hablaría con él.
erros.certo: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con él.
erros.motivo: For an unreal hypothesis, use «fuera», not «era» (English "if I WERE you").

erros.errado: Si tengo dinero, viajaría. (for an unreal hypothesis)
erros.motivo: The present after «si» names a possible condition; for an unreal hypothesis, use the imperfecto de subjuntivo.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud five things you'd do if you won the lottery: «Si ganara la lotería, yo…». Then say what you'd tell a friend who has a problem: «Yo, en tu lugar…».
Say the imperfecto de subjuntivo of «tener», «ser», «poder» and «hacer» (yo). Then say the conditional of «viajar», «tener», «hacer» and «poder» (yo): viajaría, tendría, haría, podría.
